Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. Speaking at the APEC Summit of Pacific Rim Leaders in
Xinjiang, China, President Trump used his preferred term when he spoke about artificial intelligence.
Americans invented, we just invented SI, and it is unleashing extraordinary prosperity and
growth for people all around the globe. So we do not want to do anything to destroy the

super intelligence, but we have to watch it. Trump said AI is almost completely good,
but that it's got bad elements. However, he said he opposes regulation, saying that would
stifle the industry. Trump began a one-on-one meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin
a short time ago. He is also to meet with Xi Jinping before the three sit down together
on the trilateral meeting. Trump told Fox News that it was already a win pointing to the lavish
welcome he received when he arrived in China. Homeland Security Secretary and other top
intelligence officials testified on Capitol Hill Wednesday. They were scheduled to talk about
worldwide threats since the 9/11 attacks. But NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports on the shift in focus to
more recent troubles. The senior administration officials were questioned about a string of tech
outages, most notably the rare nationwide ground stop that stranded thousands of airline passengers
Friday afternoon and into the weekend. That closely coincided with outages of Microsoft
Outlook, major banks and other services. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said that he
understood that such notable outages happening at the same time is raising questions from the
American public, but reiterated that they are all separate incidents associated with technical
problems. They are not a coordinated or state sponsored attack. The Trump administration has
been adamant that the outages are isolated and unconnected. Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Washington.
Now to the United Nations Security Council. In a new report, President Trump's Board of Peace
says Israel and Hamas are failing to meet key commitments to end the Gaza war. Linda Fisulo
reports. The Board of Peace Report offers a grim picture of progress since the ceasefire began last
November and plans for Hamas to disarm Israeli soldiers to withdraw from Gaza and to reconstruct
an action to start have stalled. It states that Israel has continued strikes against Hamas targets
and Hamas militant activity continues as the population faces another winter in tents and
rubble. The report criticizes Israel's restrictions on supplies and equipment and Hamas' taxing of
goods entering Gaza. It warns that a ceasefire without visible results cannot be sustained
indefinitely. The Board of Peace also calls on the Security Council to fully support
implementation of the plan it has endorsed for NPR News and Linda Fisulo in New York.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The city of Hollywood, Florida is one of several under a state of emergency. The emergencies were
declared Wednesday due to heavy rain that led to flooding in portions of South Florida. Preliminary
figures show a foot of rain fell in parts of Broward County. The rain caused a roof of a
synagogue to collapse and officials closed portions of the Florida Turnpike and Interstate 95 due to
high water installed vehicles. On the west coast, heavy rain and strong winds grounded planes at
San Francisco's airport disrupted ferry service and flooded roads in Napa County and other areas
in the wine country. California Scenic Highway 1 closed again in Big Sur for fear that heavy El
Nino rains expected through Thursday will send debris onto the road. The highway fully reopened
in January following three years of repair work from winter storms from member station KAZU in
Monterey. Katie Brown reports. Authorities have closed a 46-mile stretch of California's famed
Highway 1. The road between Big Sur in Monterey County and Ragged Point in San Luis Obispo County
offers panoramic views of the Pacific Ocean. Josh Silvera is a battalion chief with Cal Fire.
The last thing we would want is for somebody to be driving down the coast and then a slide
were to occur. Heavy rains are expected through the end of the day and crews will reevaluate
then for potential reopening. Silvera says it's not clear when the highway will be fully reopened
and back to normal. For NPR News, I'm Katie Brown. Asian chairs largely losing ground
